To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have determined the backbone and sidechain assignments for the human profilin-2.

The resonance assignment of human profilin II has been determined, based in triple-resonance NMR experiments using uniformly [15N, 13C]-labeled protein, and these assignments facilitate further studies on interactions of profilin II with its poly-l-prolinerich ligands.

the backbone and sidechain 15N, 1H, and 13C resonances of the human profilins I and IIa have been assigned, using a combination of triple resonance experiments and 15N and proton heteronuclear single quantum coherence (HSQC) experiments.

the structure, dynamics and function of proteins and protein complexes.

profilin IIa is the most important protein of the actin cytoskeleton in the cell.

the human G-Actin Binding Protein Profilin IIa (HGBPPIIa) is an important molecule for the actin cytoskeleton and is involved in many cellular functions such as cell motility, cell division, and cell shape.
the human profilin-IIa protein is a very stable protein with an average of 2.5% sequence variation in the human profilin family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we were able to assign the 1HN, 15N, 13Calpha, 13CO, 13CB, 13CA and 13CB resonances of 99% of the backbone amide groups, 100% of the backbone carbonyl groups, 99% of all the Cbeta groups, 98% of the alpha-carbon groups and 100% of all methyl groups of the side chain residues.
the backbone and sidechain 13C, 15N, and 1H assignments for human profilin II were obtained using triple-resonance NMR experiments on a uniformly labeled sample.
we have been able to determine the resonance assignments for the human profilin-IIa.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it provides the first backbone and side chain resonance assignments for the human profilin-IIA protein, which will be useful for the study of the interactions of profilin-IIA with its ligands.

it is possible to assign a large number of resonances in a protein that is only 13.5 kDa, and that the assignment process can be streamlined by using a combination of NMR experiments and a priori information about the protein.

the backbone and side-chain 13C chemical shifts can be used to identify and classify the different types of proline-rich sequences that bind profilins, as well as to determine the relative binding affinities for these sequences.
